tool_args.rationale: All five observations are positive and lie at H=0.16–0.48, far short of the target H=20.7. The slow-horizon probe directly tests whether the response reverses and constrains its magnitude where the forecast matters.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the dual-exponential adaptation model now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: At the pilot horizons, the slow term mainly constrains the ratio of its amplitude to its time constant. Different values can fit the pilot yet predict different signs and magnitudes at H=20.7.
Positive short-horizon gains are consistent with monotone saturation but cannot distinguish it from delayed reversal.
Finer trajectory measurements do not directly test the delayed reversal near the forecast horizon.
The auxiliary measurement does not constrain the slow adaptation component.
